linkedPullRequests.title: syncd: Skip VID-to-RID translation for FlexCounter removal
linkedPullRequests.author: Griffin-micas
linkedPullRequests.body:
Fixes sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#29260
FlexCounter removal only requires the VID, but processFlexCounterEvent currently performs VID-to-RID translation for both SET and DEL events.

When a dynamically recreated object such as PORT_SERDES is removed, its mapping may be deleted before the corresponding stop_poll event is processed. This causes a misleading missing-VID error even though the counter cleanup succeeds.

Only translate VID to RID for SET events and add a regression test ensuring DEL does not query the mapping.


<!--
Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines;
https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md

Please provide following information to help code review process a bit easier:
-->
### Description of PR
<!--
- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
- Please also include relevant motivation and context. Where should reviewer start? background context?
- List any dependencies that are required for this change.
-->

Summary:
Avoid false `processFlexCounterEvent` errors when removing FlexCounter entries whose SAI objects and VID-to-RID mappings have already been removed.

For `stop_poll`/`DEL`, FlexCounter removal only requires the VID. However, `Syncd::processFlexCounterEvent()` previously attempted VID-to-RID translation for both `SET` and `DEL`.

For dynamically recreated objects such as `SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_PORT_SERDES`, the old VID-to-RID mapping may legitimately be removed before the corresponding FlexCounter `DEL` event is processed. This produced misleading errors such as:
```
processFlexCounterEvent: port VID oid:0x57..., was not found
(probably port was removed/splitted) and will remove from counters now
```

### Type of change

<!--
- Fill x for your type of change.
- e.g.
- [x] Bug fix
-->

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
CPO platforms may register PORT_SERDES objects with the PORT_PHY_SERDES_ATTR FlexCounter group. These objects can be removed and recreated when updated SerDes parameters are applied.
The stop_poll event for the old object may therefore be processed after its VID-to-RID mapping has been removed. Since the removal path does not use the RID, attempting the translation is unnecessary and generates a misleading error.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:N/A

#### How did you do it?
Changed Syncd::processFlexCounterEvent() so that VID-to-RID translation is performed only for SET/start_poll.
The DEL/stop_poll path now directly removes the counter using the VID.
The existing SET behavior is preserved: if its VID-to-RID translation fails, Syncd logs the error and falls back to removing the stale counter entry.
Added a unit test using a mock Redis client to verify that FlexCounter removal does not call getRidForVid().

#### How did you verify/test it?
Validated on a 64-port CPO platform running docker-syncd-brcm-rpc.
Test procedure:
1. Installed the updated syncd-rpc package.
2. Restarted the syncd container.
3. Triggered the PORT_SERDES remove/recreate workflow.
4. Observed two PORT_PHY_SERDES_ATTR start_poll events.
5. Confirmed that no new processFlexCounterEvent: port VID ... was not found errors were generated.
Result:
```
post_upgrade_flexcounter_vid_errors=0
post_upgrade_serdes_start_poll_events=2
```
The last occurrence of the target error was from before the updated syncd binary was installed.
A regression unit test was also added:
```
SyncdTest.FlexCounterRemoveDoesNotRequireVidToRidTranslation
```

#### Any platform specific information?
The issue was reproduced on a Broadcom-based CPO platform where PORT_SERDES objects participate in PORT_PHY_SERDES_ATTR FlexCounter polling.
The fix is platform-independent and applies to all dynamically removed SAI object types processed by this FlexCounter path.

comments.author: Griffin-micas
comments.body:
> Correct, minimal, well-diagnosed fix — verified against the full `processFlexCounterEvent`. The root-cause analysis holds: the DEL path calls `m_manager->removeCounter(vid, groupName)`, which takes **only the VID**, so translating VID→RID on removal was doing work whose result is never consumed — and its miss produced the misleading "port VID … was not found" error for a removal that actually succeeds. For dynamically recreated objects (CPO `PORT_SERDES`) the old mapping can legitimately be gone before the `stop_poll`/DEL arrives, so gating the translation on `SET_COMMAND` is the right fix.
> 
> Details check out:
> 
> * Initializing `rid = SAI_NULL_OBJECT_ID` is necessary and also closes a latent uninitialized-read (previously `rid` was only written by `tryTranslateVidToRid`).
> * The SET-failure→DEL fallback is preserved: a native DEL now skips translation via short-circuit, while a SET that can't translate still logs and demotes to DEL exactly as before.
> * Null rid on the DEL path is never forwarded (`removeCounter` is VID-only), so it's harmless.
> * The regression test pins the right contract — `getRidForVid` called `Times(0)` on DEL — not just an incidental output.
> 
> **One request before merge: close the test-coverage gap.** The new test only exercises `fromAsicChannel = false`. The `fromAsicChannel = true` DEL branch takes an additional path (`m_flexCounterTable->del(singleKey)` + `sendApiResponse(...)`), and since the ASIC channel is exactly where the misleading ERROR was being logged (the `SWSS_LOG_ERROR` vs `SWSS_LOG_WARN` split is on `fromAsicChannel`), it's the more representative reproduction of the reported bug. Please add a second variant with `fromAsicChannel = true` asserting the same `getRidForVid` `Times(0)` + `SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS`, so both DEL branches are guarded against a future re-introduction of the translation. Everything else is approve-quality; this is the one thing I'd like tightened.
> 
> (Context: this is the third fix in this syncd FlexCounter/translator area recently — #2057 poll-guard, #2068 notification `tryTranslateRidToVid` — all sharing the same lesson: use the translator's read-only/try variants where a miss is legitimate, and don't translate where the result is unused. This is the cleanest instance.)

Thank you for the thorough review! @lolyu 
You're right — although the VID-to-RID translation gate is shared, the existing test only covers the non-ASIC-channel path. The fromAsicChannel=true variant is a more faithful reproduction of the reported issue and should also verify the FLEX_COUNTER_TABLE deletion and API response path.
I’ll add coverage for fromAsicChannel=true with the same getRidForVid Times(0) and SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS assertions, then rerun the unit tests.
